headline: 68,400-square-foot manufacturing building on Clark Avenue gets wetlands approval; residents raised flooding and traffic concerns.
summary: The plan uses a detention basin and adds wetland plantings, and the approval calls for plant inspections twice a year. Residents said water already floods basements on Matthew Street and worried about truck traffic on that road. The commission also approved a 12,250-square-foot flex storage building at 154 East Main Street, without its outside storage area.
decisions: Declared the commercial building at 225 East Main Street a significant activity.
Scheduled a December public hearing on the wetland boundary change at 59 Camp Street.
Declared the data center at 234 Riverside Avenue a significant activity and set a December public hearing.
Declared the carbon capture system at 220 Riverside Avenue a significant activity.
Approved the wetland boundary change for the flex storage building at 154 East Main Street, as presented.
Approved the wetlands permit for the flex storage building at 154 East Main Street, without the outside storage area.
Approved the floodplain permit for the flex storage building, without the outside storage area.
Approved the wetland boundary change for the 68,400-square-foot manufacturing building on Clark Avenue, with standard stipulations.
Approved the wetlands permit for the 68,400-square-foot manufacturing building on Clark Avenue, with twice-yearly plant inspections.
Approved the wetlands application for a small addition at 247 Park Street, subject to engineering stipulations.
discussion: Clark Avenue flooding and traffic: Residents said water already floods basements on Matthew Street and that trucks would add traffic. The applicant said runoff drains north, away from Matthew Street, and that the building is not in a wetland.

Outside storage at East Main Street: The commission questioned the size of the outside storage area and how its floodplain volume would be offset. Concern was raised about fuel and oil leaking from equipment onto gravel, and the outside storage was removed from the approval.
Riverside Avenue data center changes: The applicant's attorney argued the changes are not a significant activity. The commission declared them significant and set a public hearing for December.
Carbon capture gravel pad: The applicant said the 220 Riverside Avenue site would hold carbon capture equipment on a gravel pad. Staff advised the commission to act on the plan as a gravel area.
